_comment: Best-practice notes (web-researched from UE5.7 official docs) injected into ue5_python_api_reference.md by generate_api_reference.py. Edit freely; keyed by unreal class name.

notes.EditorActorSubsystem: The UE5 replacement for the deprecated unreal.EditorLevelLibrary actor/outliner functions. Get it via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorSubsystem) — never construct directly. The methods that matter: get_all_level_actors(), get_selected_level_actors()/set_selected_level_actors(list), spawn_actor_from_class(cls, location, rotation)/spawn_actor_from_object(obj, ...), duplicate_actor(actor, to_world, offset), destroy_actor()/destroy_actors(). Locations are in cm and rotations in degrees (FRotator). Gotchas: must run on the Game Thread (all UE Python does); it operates on the current editor world, so call unreal.UnrealEditorSubsystem().get_editor_world() if you need to be explicit. Spawns/deletes are individually undoable but for batches wrap in `with unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction("...")` so the Outliner coalesces redraws and the whole op is one undo. For idempotent scripts, query get_all_level_actors() and skip spawning if a matching actor already exists rather than spawn-then-dedupe. Note (5.5+): editor subsystems can throw 'Editor Subsystems can only be used in Editor Utilities' inside Scriptable Tools blueprints — fine from normal py/exec.
notes.UnrealEditorSubsystem: Tiny but essential subsystem for global editor app/world state — the UE5 home for the world/viewport-camera functions that moved off EditorLevelLibrary. Only four methods, all of which you actually use: get_editor_world() (the UWorld you edit; pass this to other subsystems that take a UWorld), get_game_world() (only non-None during PIE), and get_level_viewport_camera_info(out location, out rotation)/set_level_viewport_camera_info(location, rotation). Camera location is cm, rotation degrees. Gotcha: get_level_viewport_camera_info returns a (bool, FVector, FRotator) tuple in Python (the bool is success) — unpack accordingly. get_editor_world() is the canonical 'current world' accessor; prefer it over the deprecated unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_editor_world().
notes.LevelEditorSubsystem: Owns level-file and viewport/PIE operations (the rest of what EditorLevelLibrary did). Key methods: new_level(asset_path, is_partitioned_world=False)/new_level_from_template(), load_level(asset_path), save_current_level(), save_all_dirty_levels(), get_current_level()/set_current_level_by_name(), and the PIE controls editor_request_begin_play()/editor_request_end_play()/is_in_play_in_editor(). Also build_light_maps(quality, with_reflection_captures) and pilot/eject camera helpers. Gotchas: load_level / new_level swap the editor's current map — destructive, prompts/loses unsaved changes, and invalidates actor references you captured from the previous world, so re-query actors after a level change. Saves write to disk (slow, can trigger recompiles for level-embedded assets); guard with the dirty checks (save_all_dirty_levels already no-ops clean levels). For World Partition maps set is_partitioned_world=True on new_level. Get via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LevelEditorSubsystem).
notes.EditorAssetSubsystem: The UE5 replacement for the deprecated unreal.EditorAssetLibrary; same method names, accessed via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorAssetSubsystem). Bread-and-butter: load_asset(path), does_asset_exist(path)/do_assets_exist(list) (use these for idempotency before any rebuild), list_assets(dir, recursive, include_folder), duplicate_asset/rename_asset/delete_asset (path-string variants) and their *_loaded_asset counterparts (object variants), save_loaded_asset(asset, only_if_is_dirty=True)/save_asset(path, only_if_is_dirty=True), set_dirty_flag(obj, state), find_asset_data(path), and metadata: get_metadata_tag/set_metadata_tag/get_tag_values. Critical gotchas: keep only_if_is_dirty=True (the default) — passing False forces a disk write and can re-trigger a shader/asset recompile even when nothing changed. delete_asset cascades a recompile of every referencer, so fix up find_package_referencers_for_asset first; never delete+recreate just to re-run a script. Path-string ops (rename/duplicate/delete) don't need the asset loaded and are cheaper than loaded-object variants for bulk work. save_* persists to .uasset — without it your in-memory edits are lost on editor restart.
notes.EditorUtilitySubsystem: Runs Editor Utility Blueprints/Widgets and registers their tabs — use it to launch existing Blutility tools from script, not for general asset/actor work. Practical methods: try_run(asset)/try_run_class(cls) to execute an Editor Utility Blueprint, spawn_and_register_tab(widget_blueprint) to open an Editor Utility Widget as a docked tab, register_and_execute_task(task) for long-running UEditorUtilityTask jobs, and the tab lifecycle helpers (does_tab_exist/close_tab_by_id/unregister_tab_by_id). Gotcha: this is the entry point for 'run my EUW/EUB from Python', not a substitute for EditorActorSubsystem/EditorAssetSubsystem — most scripting needs those instead. Tabs you spawn persist in the editor UI until explicitly closed. Get via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorUtilitySubsystem).
notes.StaticMeshEditorSubsystem: Scripts the Static Mesh editor: LODs, collision, Nanite, sections, UV channels, material/mesh swaps. Get via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.StaticMeshEditorSubsystem). High-value methods: set_lods_with_notification(mesh, FStaticMeshReductionOptions, apply_changes), set_lod_group(mesh, name, rebuild_immediately=True), set_nanite_settings(mesh, FMeshNaniteSettings, apply_changes=True), add_simple_collisions_with_notification(mesh, shape_type, apply_changes)/set_convex_decomposition_collisions_with_notification(...), import_lod(mesh, lod_index, source_filename), get_lod_count/get_number_verts/get_number_materials. Critical gotcha: the apply_changes (a.k.a. rebuild_immediately) flag triggers a full mesh build + shader/derived-data rebuild — expensive and blocks the Game Thread. When changing several settings on one mesh, pass apply_changes=False on all but the last call so you rebuild once, not N times. After editing you still must EditorAssetSubsystem.save_loaded_asset() to persist. The non-notification variants (add_simple_collisions, remove_collisions, etc.) always apply immediately — prefer the *_with_notification forms for batched edits. Wrap visible edits in ScopedEditorTransaction for undo. UE5.7 deprecation: reimport_all_custom_lo_ds was renamed reimport_all_custom_lods.
notes.SkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem: Skeletal-mesh counterpart to StaticMeshEditorSubsystem: LODs, sections, sockets, physics assets, morph targets. Get via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.SkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem). Useful methods: get_lod_count/regenerate_lod(mesh, new_lod_count, ...)/import_lod/remove_lods, get_lod_build_settings/set_lod_build_settings, rename_socket(mesh, old, new), create_physics_asset(mesh, set_to_mesh=True, lod_index=0)/assign_physics_asset(mesh, physics_asset)/is_physics_asset_compatible, set_skeletal_mesh_overlay_material/set_material_slot_overlay_material, and per-section getters/setters (cast shadow, recompute tangent, visible in ray tracing) that return values via out-params (Python returns tuples — unpack the bool success plus the value). Gotcha: many getters take an out-param in C++ so in Python you read the returned tuple, e.g. ok, cast = sub.get_section_cast_shadow(mesh, lod, section). LOD regen/import rebuilds the mesh (heavy, Game Thread). Persist edits with EditorAssetSubsystem.save_loaded_asset(); wrap in ScopedEditorTransaction for undo.
notes.SubobjectDataSubsystem: The ONLY supported way to add/remove/reparent components on a Blueprint asset's component tree from script (you cannot just call add_component on a UBlueprint). It is an ENGINE subsystem: get it with unreal.get_engine_subsystem(unreal.SubobjectDataSubsystem), NOT get_editor_subsystem. Core flow: root_handle = sub.k2_gather_subobject_data_for_blueprint(blueprint)[0]; then handle, fail = sub.add_new_subobject(unreal.AddNewSubobjectParams(parent_handle=root_handle, new_class=unreal.StaticMeshComponent, blueprint_context=blueprint)); check fail.is_empty(); sub.rename_subobject(handle, unreal.Text(name)); sub.attach_subobject(root_handle, handle). Key concept: methods return/consume SubobjectDataHandle (an opaque id, NOT the component) — to get the actual component object use unreal.SubobjectDataBlueprintFunctionLibrary.get_object(get_data(handle)) and set_editor_property on it. For live actor instances (not BP assets) use k2_gather_subobject_data_for_instance(actor) and pass blueprint_context=None. Gotchas: after editing the Blueprint you must compile + EditorAssetSubsystem.save_loaded_asset() to persist; add_new_subobject does not save. add_new_subobject returns a 2-tuple (handle, fail_reason FText) — always test fail_reason.is_empty().
notes.LayersSubsystem: Manages editor visibility Layers (the Layers panel) and actor-to-layer membership. Get via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LayersSubsystem). Most-used: create_layer(name), add_actor_to_layer(actor, name)/add_actors_to_layers(actors, names), remove_actor_from_layer(...), get_actors_from_layer(name)/get_actors_from_layers(names), set_layer_visibility(name, is_visible)/make_all_layers_visible(), select_actors_in_layer(name, select, notify, ...), delete_layer/rename_layer. Gotchas: Layers are a pure editor organizational/visibility concept — they have no runtime effect and are largely superseded by the World Partition Data Layers system in partitioned maps (use Data Layers there, not this). create_layer is idempotent-friendly: check get_layer(name)/is_layer(name) first. Operates on the current editor world. Note many methods take a trailing update_stats/notify/redraw bool — leave defaults unless batching, where suppressing redraws speeds bulk edits.
notes.AssetEditorSubsystem: Opens and closes the per-asset editor windows (Material editor, BP editor, etc.) — UI control only, not asset data editing. Get via unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.AssetEditorSubsystem). The methods you need: open_editor_for_assets(list_of_loaded_objects) to pop open editor tabs, close_all_editors_for_asset(obj), close_all_asset_editors(), and find_editor_for_asset/get_all_edited_assets for introspection. Gotcha: takes loaded UObjects (EditorAssetSubsystem.load_asset(path) first), not path strings. Don't confuse with EditorAssetSubsystem (data ops) — this one just manages windows. Opening editors spins up Slate UI on the Game Thread; for headless/batch asset processing you almost never want this, edit the asset object directly and save instead. Useful to force an asset's editor closed before a destructive rename/delete so stale tabs don't linger.
notes.EditorActorFolders: WARNING: this class is NOT exposed to the Python API in UE5.7 — unreal.EditorActorFolders does not exist (the underlying FActorFolders is a plain C++ struct accessed via FActorFolders::Get(), not a UObject/subsystem, and its old FName-based CreateFolder/DeleteFolder/RenameFolderInWorld methods were deprecated in 5.0 in favor of FFolder). Do not try to get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorFolders) — it will raise. To organize actors into Outliner folders from Python, set the folder path directly on each actor: actor.set_folder_path(unreal.Name('Parent/Child')) (or set_folder_path_recursively); read it back with actor.get_folder_path(). Creating a folder is implicit — assigning a path that doesn't exist yet creates it. For World Partition maps, folders are persisted as UActorFolder objects automatically when you set actor folder paths.
notes.AssetToolsHelpers: Thin accessor only: call `unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()` once to get the singleton `AssetTools` object — that returned object is where the real work lives (`create_asset(name, package_path, asset_class, factory)`, `create_unique_asset_name(base_package_name, suffix)`, `duplicate_asset(name, path, source_obj)`, `rename_assets`/`rename_assets_with_dialog`, `import_assets`/`import_asset_tasks`). For idempotent scripts, ALWAYS guard `create_asset` with `unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(...)` and `load_asset` the existing one instead — `create_asset` over an existing path can clobber or error. Use `create_unique_asset_name` to dodge collisions in batch creation. In headless/commandlet automation NEVER use the `*_with_dialog` variants (they block); pick factories that import unattended (e.g. avoid the interactive `FbxFactory` dialog). Must run on the game thread; new assets are dirty-in-memory — persist with `EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset` or `save_loaded_asset` afterward.
notes.AssetRegistryHelpers: The query/inspection layer for UNLOADED assets — pairs with `unreal.AssetRegistryHelpers.get_asset_registry()` (returns the `AssetRegistry` where `get_assets_by_path`/`get_assets_by_class`/`get_all_assets`/`get_referencers`/`run_assets_discovery_gathering` live). The helper itself operates on `FAssetData`: `get_asset(asset_data)` (loads on demand), `get_class`, `to_soft_object_path`, `get_tag_value`, `is_valid`, `is_redirector`, `is_u_asset`, plus `get_blueprint_assets`/`get_derived_class_asset_data`/`find_asset_native_class` for BP-class hierarchy queries without loading. Bridge from a path via `EditorAssetLibrary.find_asset_data(path)`. KEY WIN: reading tag values and classes here is cheap because it does NOT load the asset (avoid the shader/asset-load cost of `load_asset`). Gotcha: on a cold editor the registry may still be scanning — results can be incomplete until discovery finishes; tag/dependency data can have false positives until all assets are loaded+resaved. UE5.7 deprecation: the bool-argument `get_assets_with_outer_for_paths(...)` overload is deprecated in favor of the enum-flags overload.
notes.EditorAssetLibrary: The everyday content-browser workhorse for load/save/exist/list/duplicate/rename/delete on assets BY PATH (it auto-loads as needed). The four that matter: `does_asset_exist(path)` (your idempotency guard — check before any expensive rebuild), `load_asset(path)`, `save_asset(path, only_if_is_dirty=True)` / `save_loaded_asset(obj, only_if_is_dirty=True)`, and `list_assets(dir, recursive, include_folder)`. Also `duplicate_asset`, `rename_asset`, `delete_asset`, `find_asset_data` (bridge to AssetRegistryHelpers), and metadata get/set tag helpers. Critical gotchas: `only_if_is_dirty` defaults True — leave it (passing False forces a disk write + recompile every run); `save_asset` already triggers any needed recompile, so do not also call `recompile_material`/`update_material_instance`. ALL operations are slow, must run on the game thread, do NOT work in PIE, and do NOT work on level assets (use EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils/LevelEditorSubsystem for maps). `delete_asset` cascades recompiles onto every referencer — fix up referencers first and never delete just to re-create (breaks idempotency). UE5.7 note: Epic increasingly steers editor scripting toward `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorAssetSubsystem)`, which mirrors this API 1:1 and is the forward-looking choice; this BlueprintFunctionLibrary remains supported.
notes.MaterialEditingLibrary: The only sanctioned way to build/edit Material graphs and tweak MaterialInstanceConstants from Python. Core flow: `create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionX, x, y)` to add nodes, `connect_material_expressions(from, from_out, to, to_in)` (empty-string out/in names = first pin) and `connect_material_property(from, out_name, unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)` to wire to outputs, then exactly ONE `recompile_material(material)` at the end. For MICs use the `set_material_instance_*_parameter_value` setters; for the parent use `set_material_instance_parent` (guard it — reparenting to the same asset still forces a full MI shader rebuild; compare `mi.get_editor_property('parent')` first). Match `sampler_type` on TextureSample nodes to the texture's compression (Metal/SM6 rejects mismatches at compile). Heavy gotchas: every graph mutation can kick a shader compile — batch all node edits then recompile once; the per-MIC scalar setter `set_material_instance_static_switch_parameter_value` has a `b_update_material_instance` flag so you can defer the rebuild and call `update_material_instance` once. Material edits must dirty packages on the game thread (`create_material_expression_ex` exposes `b_allow_marking_package_dirty`). Some hidden material properties (e.g. WorldPositionOffset) aren't in the `MaterialProperty` enum — needs a workaround lib. Saving the material recompiles, so don't double-compile.
notes.BlueprintEditorLibrary: Edits Blueprint ASSETS (the editor-only `UBlueprint`, not the runtime CDO/instance) — graphs, functions, variables, reparenting. Most-used: `compile_blueprint(bp)` (run after any structural change or the generated class is stale), `create_blueprint_asset_with_parent(asset_path, parent_class)`, `add_member_variable(bp, name, pin_type)` / `add_member_variable_with_value`, and `generated_class(bp)` to get the UClass for spawning/CDO work. Helpers: `get_blueprint_asset(obj)`/`get_blueprint_for_class(cls)` to go between asset and class, `find_event_graph`/`find_graph`/`add_function_graph`/`remove_unused_nodes`/`remove_unused_variables`, `reparent_blueprint`, and `set_blueprint_variable_expose_on_spawn`/`_instance_editable`/`_expose_to_cinematics`. Build pin types with `get_basic_type_by_name`/`get_struct_type`/`get_object_reference_type`/`get_array_type` etc. Gotchas: to read/write a variable's DEFAULT value you go through `generated_class().get_default_object()`, NOT this library; `remove_function_graph` does NOT fix up call sites. Must run on game thread, mark dirty + `EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset` to persist, and always `compile_blueprint` before relying on the new class. UE5.7 adds asset-save-version utilities here (`compare_asset_save_version_to`, `get_saved_by_engine_version`, `get_current_engine_version`) for upgrade tooling.
notes.DataTableFunctionLibrary: Read and (editor-only) rewrite DataTables/CurveTables. Read side (works at runtime too): `get_data_table_row_names`, `get_data_table_column_names`, `does_data_table_row_exist`, `get_data_table_row_struct`, `get_data_table_column_as_string`. Editor-only bulk I/O: `fill_data_table_from_csv_string`/`_csv_file`/`_json_string`/`_json_file` (these EMPTY then refill the whole table — pass the optional `import_row_struct` to force a fully automated import with no dialogs/questions, essential for headless runs) and the matching `export_data_table_to_csv/json_string/file`. Row-level editor ops: `add_data_table_row`/`remove_data_table_row`. Gotchas: column names returned are RAW property names, not the friendly CSV/JSON export names — convert via `get_data_table_column_name_from_export_name`. `add_data_table_row` and `get_data_table_row_from_name` are CustomThunk wildcard nodes — from Python you must pass a struct instance whose type matches the table's row struct or it silently fails. Mutations only take in `WITH_EDITOR`, must run on the game thread, and you must mark the package dirty + `EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset` to persist. `fill_*` returning False means check the Output Log for the import error.
notes.EditorUtilityLibrary: Glue for selection-driven and Editor Utility Widget (Blutility) tools — answers 'what is the user currently pointing at?'. Most-used: `get_selected_assets()` / `get_selected_assets_of_class(cls)` / `get_selected_asset_data()` (content browser selection), `get_selection_set()` (selected ACTORS in the level) and `get_selection_bounds`, plus `get_selected_folder_paths`/`get_current_content_browser_path` for context-aware scripts. Also `sync_browser_to_folders`, a quick `rename_asset(asset, new_name)` (in-place rename only, cannot move folders — use AssetTools/EditorAssetLibrary to relocate), and widget-blueprint authoring helpers (`add_source_widget`, `find_source_widget_by_name`, `convert_to_editor_utility_widget`). The async action classes in the same header (`AsyncEditorDelay`, `AsyncWaitForGameWorld`) let Blutility graphs wait frames/seconds. Gotchas: everything is `WITH_EDITOR`-only and game-thread; selection getters return a live snapshot so capture once at the top of a script rather than re-querying mid-loop; pair with `unreal.EditorUtilitySubsystem` to spawn/run the widgets themselves.
notes.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils: Map-level and bulk-package load/save — the piece EditorAssetLibrary deliberately can't do (it refuses level assets). The two that matter for pipelines: `save_dirty_packages(save_map_packages, save_content_packages)` (call once at the END of a batch with both True to flush everything modified) and `load_map(filename)` (force-load, no prompts — the automation-safe variant). Also `save_packages(packages, only_dirty)` for an explicit list, `save_map(world, asset_path)` / `save_current_level`, and `import_scene`/`export_scene`. Gotchas: the `*_with_dialog` variants (`load_map_with_dialog`, `new_map_from_dialog`) BLOCK on UI and will hang or fail in commandlet/headless runs — never use them unattended. Must run on the game thread. For new editor work Epic favors `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LevelEditorSubsystem).load_level(path)` for loading; this class's `save_dirty_packages(True, True)` is still the canonical end-of-script save. Load the map BEFORE you mutate/save it in render/build pipelines. (Niche helpers like file-dialog pickers exist but rarely belong in scripts.)
notes.SystemLibrary: Maps to C++ UKismetSystemLibrary (Kismet/KismetSystemLibrary.h) — the generic 'utility' grab-bag: validity checks, console commands, traces, debug draw, timers. In editor Python the few methods that earn their keep are `is_valid(object)` (guard before touching possibly-GC'd UObjects), `get_object_name(object)`, and `execute_console_command(world_context_object, command, specific_player=None)` for things with no Python binding (e.g. `r.*` cvars, `obj gc`). Almost every method takes a `world_context_object` first arg: in editor scripts pass `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.UnrealEditorSubsystem).get_editor_world()` (or any actor) — passing None silently no-ops or errors. GOTCHAS: the trace family (`line_trace_single`, `sphere_trace_single`, etc.) needs a live PIE/game world to hit anything — they return False against a cold editor world with no physics scene, so don't use them for editor geometry queries (use line traces via the world or EditorActorSubsystem instead). Anything latent — `delay`, `retriggerable_delay`, `k2_set_timer*` — is built on the game tick and will NOT fire from a one-shot editor `exec` script; never `delay()` in editor tooling, it just discards the latent action. `print_string` writes to the PIE viewport+log; for editor scripts prefer `unreal.log/log_warning/log_error` so output lands in the LogPython category. Runs on the game thread like all unreal Python.
notes.GameplayStatics: Maps to C++ UGameplayStatics (Kismet/GameplayStatics.h) — the runtime/gameplay façade: spawn actors, fetch player/pawn/controller/game-mode, play sounds, apply damage, open levels, world time. Most useful in Python: `spawn_actor_from_class(world_context_object, actor_class, location, rotation, ...)`, `get_all_actors_of_class(world_context, actor_class)` / `get_actor_of_class(...)`, `get_player_controller(world_context, index)`, `get_time_seconds(world_context)`. EVERY call needs a real world as `world_context_object`; in editor get it via `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.UnrealEditorSubsystem).get_editor_world()`. CRITICAL EDITOR GOTCHA: prefer `unreal.EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_class(actor_class, location, rotation)` over GameplayStatics for editor tooling — the EditorActorSubsystem path registers the actor with the editor (selection, transactions/undo, marks the level dirty so it persists on save), whereas GameplayStatics spawns a runtime-style actor that the editor doesn't properly track and that won't survive a save cleanly. Pass the class object directly (`unreal.StaticMeshActor` or a loaded BP's `generated_class()`), never `unreal.Class(name=...)`. `get_all_actors_of_class` is O(all actors) — cache the result, don't call it in a loop. Player/pawn/game-mode getters return None outside PIE. `get_all_actors_of_class` is fine read-only; spawn/destroy mutate the level so wrap batches in `unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction` and save the level afterward. Units: cm for location, degrees for FRotator. `begin_spawning_actor_from_blueprint` is deprecated — use the deferred `begin_deferred_actor_spawn_from_class` + `finish_spawning_actor` pair if you need to set properties before BeginPlay.
notes.MathLibrary: Maps to C++ UKismetMathLibrary (Kismet/KismetMathLibrary.h) — pure, stateless math: vector/rotator/transform/quat ops, interpolation, random, type conversions, easing. No world context, no game-thread mutation, no save concerns — safe to call freely. In Python you rarely need it: native `unreal.Vector`/`unreal.Rotator`/`unreal.Transform`/`unreal.Quat` already overload `+ - * /`, `.length()`, `.normal()`, `.rotation()`, etc., and Python's own `math`/`random` cover scalars, so reach for MathLibrary only for the gameplay-flavored helpers that have no native equivalent: `find_look_at_rotation(start, target)`, `make_rot_from_x/xz(...)`, the `*_interp_to(current, target, delta_time, speed)` family (frame-rate-correct smoothing — needs a real delta-time, meaningless in a one-shot editor script), `random_unit_vector_in_cone_in_degrees(...)`, and `ease(...)`. GOTCHAS: all angles are DEGREES (`make_rotator`, `find_look_at_rotation`), distances cm; `random_*` here draws from the shared engine RNG (non-deterministic across runs) — for reproducible/idempotent generation seed `random.Random(seed)` in Python or use `unreal.MathLibrary.random_*_from_stream` with an explicit `RandomStream`. The many `conv_*` methods are autogenerated Blueprint cast nodes — in Python just construct the target type directly instead.
notes.KismetRenderingLibrary: Maps to C++ UKismetRenderingLibrary (Kismet/KismetRenderingLibrary.h) — render-target authoring/capture: create/clear/resize RTs, bake a material into an RT, draw via Canvas, read back pixels, export to disk, and (editor-only) convert an RT into a persistent UTexture2D. Workhorses for tooling: `create_render_target2d(world_context, w, h, format=RTF_RGBA16f, clear_color, auto_gen_mips, support_uavs)`, `draw_material_to_render_target(world_context, render_target, material)` (one-shot bake — internally a flush+draw; this is shader/GPU work, the expensive part), and the EDITOR-ONLY bake-out `render_target_create_static_texture2d_editor_only(render_target, name, compression_settings=TC_Default, mip_settings)`. For many draws into one RT use the `begin_draw_canvas_to_render_target` / `end_draw_canvas_to_render_target` pair (each `draw_material_to_render_target` does its own setup/flush — don't loop it). GOTCHAS: all calls need a valid `world_context_object` (editor: `UnrealEditorSubsystem.get_editor_world()`). An RT created via `create_render_target2d` is TRANSIENT — it vanishes on editor restart; to persist visuals you must convert to a UTexture2D (`*_editor_only`) or `export_render_target(...)` to a file, then save the asset. Match `format` to need: `RTF_RGBA8` for color, a float format (RTF_RGBA16f/RTF_R16f) when you read back HDR/linear data via `read_render_target_raw_pixel`. Pixel readback (`read_render_target*`) stalls the game thread on a GPU fence — slow, avoid per-pixel loops; use the bulk `read_render_target_raw(out_samples)`. The `*_editor_only` and `convert_render_target_to_texture2d_editor_only` functions exist only in editor builds. Game thread; this triggers real GPU/shader work so wrap long sequences in ScopedSlowTask and flush via the project's shader-progress helper when timing matters.
notes.KismetMaterialLibrary: Maps to C++ UKismetMaterialLibrary (Kismet/KismetMaterialLibrary.h) — two distinct jobs: (1) create runtime-tweakable Dynamic Material Instances, and (2) read/write Material Parameter Collection (MPC) globals. Key methods: `create_dynamic_material_instance(world_context, parent, optional_name=NAME_None, creation_flags=EMIDCreationFlags.NONE)` returns a UMaterialInstanceDynamic you then drive with `mid.set_scalar_parameter_value/set_vector_parameter_value/set_texture_parameter_value`; and the MPC pair `set_scalar_parameter_value(world_context, collection, param_name, value)` / `set_vector_parameter_value(...)` plus the `get_*` readers. GOTCHAS: a DMI is a TRANSIENT runtime object — do NOT use it for editor authoring you want to persist. For permanent material edits create/save a real UMaterialInstanceConstant (via AssetTools / `set_material_instance_parent` + `MaterialEditingLibrary.set_material_instance_*_parameter_value`) and save the asset; a DMI is only for live, in-PIE/game tweaks and is thrown away. MPC `set_*_parameter_value` writes a GLOBAL shared by every material sampling that collection — changes are not per-instance and (in editor) won't persist unless you edit and save the MPC asset itself. All five take a `world_context_object` (editor: `UnrealEditorSubsystem.get_editor_world()`). MPC param names must exactly match the collection's defined Scalar/Vector entries or the call silently does nothing. Game thread; setting parameters is cheap (no recompile) — unlike editing the parent material graph, which forces shader recompiles.
notes.Actor: Base class for everything placeable in a level; in editor scripting you usually get these from `get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorSubsystem)` (NOT the deprecated `EditorLevelLibrary`/`EditorActorUtilities` legacy functions). The methods that matter: `get_actor_location/set_actor_location`, `set_actor_transform`, `get_component_by_class`, and reading/writing any UPROPERTY via `get_editor_property`/`set_editor_property` (prefer these over raw attribute assignment so PostEditChange fires and the actor is marked dirty). Units are cm and degrees. GOTCHA: every mutation runs on the game thread, so wrap edits in `with unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction('label'):` so they land on the undo stack and the editor coalesces redraws; call the actor's `modify()` before changing it if you want robust transaction tracking. Spawn via `EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_object/spawn_actor_from_class`. To persist level changes you must save the level/map, not `save_asset`.
notes.StaticMeshActor: A thin level actor wrapping a single UStaticMesh; the renderer's cheapest geometry path. You almost never set its mesh on the actor directly — grab its `static_mesh_component` (the root) and call `set_static_mesh(mesh)` / `set_material(idx, mtl)` on that. Spawn with `EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_object(static_mesh_asset, location, rotation)` which returns a ready StaticMeshActor. GOTCHA: meshes dragged from the Content Browser auto-become StaticMeshActors, so when querying a level use `EditorActorSubsystem.get_all_level_actors()` + filter by class rather than assuming type. Mobility defaults to Static — to move it at runtime/PIE you must set the component's `mobility` to Movable first. Wrap placement in `ScopedEditorTransaction`; save the level to persist.
notes.StaticMeshComponent: The render+collision component that holds a StaticMesh asset reference plus per-instance material overrides. Key methods: `set_static_mesh(mesh)` (verified in UE5.7 headers, returns bool), and inherited `set_material(index, material_interface)` / `get_material(index)` / `get_num_materials()` for per-instance overrides that do NOT touch the source asset. GOTCHA: overrides set here live on the component, not the StaticMesh — to change the asset's default materials edit the StaticMesh's `static_materials` instead. Changing the mesh on a component whose `mobility` is Static while the actor is in a built world can require a registration refresh; for editor scripts it's fine. All transform/visibility edits go through its SceneComponent base (set_world_location etc.) on the game thread inside a transaction.
notes.SceneComponent: Base for any component with a transform and an attachment hierarchy; this is where ALL placement methods live (StaticMesh/Skeletal/Primitive components inherit them). The four that matter: `set_world_location(loc, sweep=False, teleport=False)`, `set_relative_transform(t)`, `set_world_transform(t)`, and `attach_to_component(parent, socket, ...)`. Units are cm/degrees; `relative_*` is parent-space, `world_*` is absolute. GOTCHAS: `sweep`/`teleport` only matter when physics/collision is on (default both False for editor placement — sweep can silently block movement); these MUST run on the game thread (use `unreal.PythonBPLib.exec_python_command(cmd, force_game_thread=True)` if you're ever off-thread). Wrap in `ScopedEditorTransaction` for undo. `relative_scale3d` is local-space only (no shear).
notes.PrimitiveComponent: Intermediate base (between SceneComponent and mesh components) that adds rendering, collision, and the material slot API. The header-verified methods are `set_material(element_index, material)`, `get_material(element_index)`, and `get_num_materials()` — this is THE place per-component material overrides actually live, inherited by Static/Skeletal/Instanced mesh components. Also exposes collision (`set_collision_enabled`, `set_collision_profile_name`), visibility, and physics simulation toggles. GOTCHA: setting a material here overrides only this one component instance and does not dirty the underlying mesh asset; if you want the change to persist for all users of the mesh, edit the asset's material array instead. Editor edits need the game thread + a transaction to be undoable.
notes.StaticMesh: The on-disk geometry asset. Materials are exposed as the `static_materials` property — an Array[StaticMaterial] (header: BlueprintGetter GetStaticMaterials / BlueprintSetter SetStaticMaterials). To change a slot you must copy the array out, mutate, and set it back (TArray editor-bug pattern): `mats = mesh.get_static_materials(); mats[0].material_interface = mtl; mesh.set_static_materials(mats)`. Bounds via `get_bounding_box()`. UE5.7 DEPRECATION: do NOT touch the `nanite_settings` member directly (header marks it `UE_DEPRECATED(5.7)`) — use `get_nanite_settings()`/the editor-property accessor instead. GOTCHA: editing this asset and saving triggers a build+recompile of dependent materials; `save_asset` already recompiles, so don't double-call build/recompile. Be idempotent — guard with `does_asset_exist` and skip if already configured. Game thread only.
notes.SkeletalMesh: Bone-driven deformable mesh asset. Unlike StaticMesh there is no simple set_material(index) on the asset — materials live in the `materials` property, an Array[SkeletalMaterial] struct (fields: `material_interface`, `material_slot_name`, read-only `imported_material_slot_name`, `uv_channel_data`). Reassign via the copy-out/edit/set-back pattern: `m = sk.get_editor_property('materials'); m[0].set_editor_property('material_interface', mtl); sk.set_editor_property('materials', m)`. Also exposes `skeleton` and `physics_asset` properties — a common validation script is finding skeletal meshes with no physics_asset (causes ragdoll/shadow/visibility bugs). GOTCHA: `material_interface` needs a LOADED MaterialInterface object, never a string path. Save with `save_loaded_asset` on the game thread; per-instance overrides go on a SkeletalMeshComponent, not here.
notes.MaterialInterface: Abstract base of both Material and MaterialInstance — this is the type you pass to any `set_material(idx, ...)` call, so write functions to accept MaterialInterface, not the concrete subclass. Useful read methods: `get_base_material()` (header-confirmed; walks the instance chain to the root Material) and the parameter getters (`get_scalar_parameter_value` etc.). GOTCHA: you cannot author/edit a material through this base — to change parameters you need a MaterialInstanceConstant (use MaterialEditingLibrary) or to edit the Material graph itself. When reading a component/mesh's assigned material you get back a MaterialInterface; load instances/materials with `load_asset` (returns the right subclass) before assigning.
notes.MaterialInstanceConstant: The editor-time (baked, non-runtime) material instance asset — the workhorse for asset pipelines. NEVER set its parent or parameters by raw property assignment; use `unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary`: `set_material_instance_parent(mi, parent)`, then `set_material_instance_scalar/vector/texture_parameter_value(mi, name, value)`. CRITICAL ORDER: set the parent FIRST — available parameters are inherited from the parent and only exposed (named) parameters can be set; param names must match exactly (case + spaces). IDEMPOTENCY GOTCHA: reparenting to the SAME asset still forces a full MI shader rebuild, so guard with `if mi.get_editor_property('parent') != new_parent:` before reparenting. `set_material_instance_parent` already refreshes the MI and `save_asset` already recompiles — do not also call update_material_instance/recompile_material (double compile). Match texture `sampler_type` to the texture's compression. For runtime parameter changes use MaterialInstanceDynamic instead. Game thread only.
notes.Material: The root material asset that owns the actual shader graph (expression nodes). In Python you rarely build the graph by hand — when you must, use `unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary` (`create_material_expression`, `connect_material_property`, `connect_material_expressions`) plus `recompile_material`. Most pipelines instead create a hand-authored parent Material once and drive looks via MaterialInstanceConstants. KEY RULE: only nodes that are named Scalar/Vector/Texture *Parameter* expressions are settable on child instances — plain Constant nodes are invisible to instances. GOTCHA: every graph edit forces a shader compile (the slowest editor operation); duplicating a 30-expression material recompiles all 30, so prefer adding a static switch to the existing parent over duplicate-and-edit. Compiles can block the UI for seconds — wrap in ScopedSlowTask and flush via the shared `wait_for_shaders` helper. Game thread only.
notes.Texture2D: Standard 2D texture asset. For scripting, the load-bearing properties are `compression_settings` (TC_* enum) and `srgb` — you must READ these (`get_editor_property`) when wiring a texture onto a material sampler, because Metal/SM6 reject sampler/compression mismatches at shader-compile time (e.g. TC_ALPHA must use SAMPLERTYPE_ALPHA, TC_NORMALMAP must use NORMAL). Don't guess the sampler; drive it from the texture. Export via `unreal.RenderingLibrary.export_texture2d(world, tex, dir, name)` but note it warns 'Unsupported source texture format' and writes a 0kb file when source data isn't a supported format — exporting a render target is more reliable. GOTCHA: after changing texture properties call save (which rebuilds); editing compression triggers a rebuild of the texture and recompiles dependent materials. Game thread only.
notes.TextureRenderTarget2D: GPU render target for off-screen rendering and image export. Create with `unreal.RenderingLibrary.create_render_target2d(world, w, h, format=...)`; export with `export_render_target(world, rt, dir, name)` — output format (PNG vs .HDR) is chosen by the RT's `render_target_format`, NOT the filename extension (LDR->PNG/sRGB, HDR float->.HDR/linear). Pick the SMALLEST sufficient format: RTF_RGBA32f costs 16x the memory/bandwidth of RTF_R8. GOTCHAS: hold a Python reference to the RT or it gets garbage-collected mid-use; always pair `begin_draw_canvas_to_render_target` with `end_draw_canvas_to_render_target`; avoid the per-pixel `read_render_target*` functions for bulk export (flagged 'incredibly inefficient'). To persist as a reusable asset use the editor-only `render_target_create_static_texture2d_editor_only` (requires power-of-two, 4 channels). Color space: set `srgb`/`target_gamma` deliberately. Game thread only.
notes.Blueprint: The Blueprint ASSET (an unreal.Blueprint), which is a different type from the unreal.Actor/class it generates — to spawn instances or read defaults you go through its `generated_class`, not the Blueprint object itself. Create with `BlueprintFactory` (set `parent_class`) + `AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(...)`. Add components NOT via legacy APIs but via `unreal.get_engine_subsystem(unreal.SubobjectDataSubsystem)`: gather the root handle (`k2_gather_subobject_data_for_blueprint`), `add_new_subobject(AddNewSubobjectParams(parent_handle, new_class, blueprint_context))`, check the returned `fail_reason` is empty, then `rename_subobject`/`attach_subobject`; resolve handle->object with `SubobjectDataBlueprintFunctionLibrary.get_object`. CRITICAL: after any structural/default edit call `unreal.BlueprintEditorLibrary.compile_blueprint(bp)` then `save_loaded_asset(bp)` — the CDO is rebuilt on compile. Use `set_editor_property` on the CDO so changes dirty correctly. Avoid `add_new_blueprint_component` in automation (it prompts the user). Game thread only.
notes.DataAsset: Lightweight UObject for designer/config data (no graph, no level placement). Create with `unreal.DataAssetFactory` — set its `data_asset_class` to your subclass — then `AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(name, '/Game/Path', YourClass, factory)`. Populate via `set_editor_property('prop', value)` (NOT raw attribute assignment): this fires PreEdit/PostEditChange and marks the asset dirty so it actually saves. ARRAY GOTCHA: due to a long-standing editor bug you cannot mutate a TArray property in place — copy to a Python list, edit, then `set_editor_property` the whole list back. Save with `EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(path)`/`save_loaded_asset`. PrimaryDataAsset is the AssetManager-loadable variant (implements GetPrimaryAssetId, auto-updates AssetBundleData on save). Be idempotent: guard with `does_asset_exist` and skip recreation. Game thread only.
notes.DirectionalLightComponent: The sun: parallel-ray light, almost always the atmosphere sun. Inherits `intensity` from LightComponentBase — units are LUX when the light uses physical units (default), so daylight is ~75000-120000, NOT a 0-10 multiplier; set with `set_intensity()` and `set_light_color()`/`light_color`. To drive the sky/clouds it must be the atmosphere light: check/set `atmosphere_sun_light` (bool) and `atmosphere_sun_light_index` (0=sun, 1=moon) via `set_atmosphere_sun_light()`/`set_atmosphere_sun_light_index()`. Control the sun's position by rotating the OWNING ACTOR's transform (degrees) — the component direction follows the actor's forward vector; there is no `set_direction`. Gotchas: runs on the game thread; wrap actor-rotation + property edits in `unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction` and call `modify()` before mutating, then `save` the level to persist; `light_source_angle` (deg, default 0.5357 = real sun) softens shadows and the visual sun disk. After moving the sun, any non-realtime SkyLight and any reflection captures are stale and must be recaptured/rebuilt separately. `bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight` is deprecated — use `bAtmosphereSunLight`.
notes.SkyLightComponent: Ambient/diffuse + specular environment lighting captured from the sky into a cubemap. The single most important decision is `real_time_capture` vs manual recapture: prefer enabling it via `set_real_time_capture(True)` (the `real_time_capture`/`source_type`/`cubemap` properties are BlueprintReadOnly, so you CANNOT assign them with `set_editor_property` — you must use the setters `set_real_time_capture`, `set_cubemap`, `set_source_cubemap_angle`). Real-time capture stays on GPU, auto-accounts for SkyAtmosphere+VolumetricCloud, and removes the need to recapture. `recapture_sky()` (NOT `recapture_sky_light`) is the Python name for the manual scene recapture — it is VERY costly (~120ms hitch) and only needed for non-realtime sky lights after you change the sun, sky material, or a SpecifiedCubemap; call it ONCE after batching all edits, never per-property. Use `set_intensity()`/`set_light_color()`/`set_indirect_lighting_intensity()` for energy (intensity scales existing capture cheaply, no recapture). For day/night transitions on a SpecifiedCubemap use `set_cubemap_blend(src, dst, frac)` instead of repeated recaptures. `set_brightness()` is DEPRECATED → use `set_intensity()`. Game-thread only; wrap in ScopedEditorTransaction + modify() and save to persist. `cubemap_resolution` must be a power of two.
notes.SkyAtmosphereComponent: Physically-based planetary atmosphere driving sky color, aerial perspective, and (with a realtime SkyLight) ambient color. Almost every property is BlueprintReadOnly, so mutate through the dedicated setters, not `set_editor_property`: `set_rayleigh_scattering_scale`, `set_mie_scattering_scale`, `set_mie_anisotropy`, `set_multi_scattering_factor`, `set_sky_luminance_factor`, `set_aerial_pespective_view_distance_scale` (note Epic's spelling 'Pespective'), etc. CRITICAL UNITS: `bottom_radius` (ground radius) and `atmosphere_height` are in KILOMETERS (default ground ~6360 km, height ~60 km) — passing centimeters yields a black/broken sky. Tent-distribution and scattering altitudes are also km; elevation angles are degrees. The sun is owned by the DirectionalLight, but `override_atmosphere_light_direction(index, dir)` lets you DECOUPLE the visual sun disk/scattering direction from the actual light actor — remember `reset_atmosphere_light_direction_override(index)` to re-link. Utility `get_atmospheric_light_to_match_illuminance_on_ground(dir, lux)` computes the outer-space directional-light intensity needed for a target ground illuminance — use it to set the sun's intensity correctly. Game-thread; transaction + modify() + save. Setters mark the component dirty and the LUTs rebuild on the next tick (cheap, GPU); no explicit recapture needed for the atmosphere itself, but a non-realtime SkyLight reading it is then stale.
notes.PostProcessVolume: Actor (AVolume) that applies post-process settings either inside its bounds or globally. The single biggest gotcha: ALL the actual effect values live in the `settings` struct (`unreal.PostProcessSettings`, accessed via `get_editor_property('settings')`), and every one is gated by an `override_*` bool — e.g. to change exposure you must set BOTH `settings.override_auto_exposure_bias=True` AND `settings.auto_exposure_bias=...`; the value is silently ignored otherwise. Because the struct is a value type, after mutating it you MUST write it back: `ppv.set_editor_property('settings', settings)`. Use `bUnbound`/`unbound=True` for a world-wide volume, plus `priority` (higher wins on overlap), `blend_weight` (0-1), and `bEnabled`. Note `auto_exposure_bias` default is 1.0 in new volumes (Epic changed it from 0.0 because 0 looked too dark). `add_or_update_blendable(material, weight)` attaches a post-process material. Game-thread; wrap edits in ScopedEditorTransaction + actor modify(), and save the level. No recapture/rebuild needed — changes are live in the editor viewport immediately.
notes.SphereReflectionCapture: Placeable actor that captures a static cubemap of its surroundings for cheap, pre-baked specular reflections within a sphere of influence (Lumen/SSR can replace it, but captures remain the zero-runtime-cost fallback). The actor itself is a thin wrapper — almost everything you tune lives on its `SphereReflectionCaptureComponent` (`capture_component`): `influence_radius` (cm, the sphere that receives this reflection — UIMin 8, UIMax 16384), `brightness`, `cubemap`, and `reflection_source_type` (CapturedScene vs SpecifiedCubemap). CRITICAL: there is NO per-actor/per-component Python method to recapture — the component's recapture functions are not BlueprintCallable. To bake/refresh ALL reflection captures in the level you must call `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LevelEditorSubsystem).build_light_maps(quality, with_reflection_captures=True)` (or the editor 'Build Reflection Captures' command); captures are stale and show stale lighting until then. Spawn with `EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_class(unreal.SphereReflectionCapture, location)`. Game-thread; transaction + modify() + save. Moving the sun/sky invalidates every capture — rebuild after lighting changes.
notes.ReflectionCaptureComponent: Abstract base for the shape-specific capture components (Sphere/Box/Plane); you never instantiate it directly — use `SphereReflectionCaptureComponent`/`BoxReflectionCaptureComponent`. Holds the shared knobs: `brightness` (scales captured reflection intensity, UIMin 0.5 / UIMax 4), `cubemap` + `reflection_source_type` (CapturedScene or SpecifiedCubemap), `source_cubemap_angle`, and `capture_offset`. Key gotcha for scripting: like the actor, it exposes NO BlueprintCallable/Python recapture method — the C++ `MarkDirtyForRecapture` and `UpdateReflectionCaptureContents` are not bound to Python. Editing `brightness`/`cubemap` from Python changes the stored values but the on-screen reflection only refreshes after a level-wide rebuild via `LevelEditorSubsystem.build_light_maps(..., with_reflection_captures=True)`. Subclass-specific influence (`influence_radius` on the sphere) determines which surfaces receive this capture. Game-thread; transaction + modify() + save.
notes.Landscape: The ALandscape *manager* actor (one per landscape, subclass of LandscapeProxy) that owns the editor edit-layer system and the loaded proxies; reach it via get_all_actors_of_class, not by spawning. In UE5.7 every landscape uses edit layers (non-edit-layer landscapes are deprecated this version), so heightmap/weightmap mutation goes through CreateLayer/CopyDataToEditLayer plus the LandscapeImportHeightmapFromRenderTarget(rt, import_height_from_rg_channel, edit_layer_index) inherited from LandscapeProxy. render_heightmap(world_transform, extents, out_render_target) and render_weightmap(s)(...) read the merged result top-down into an RTF_RGBA16f/32f render target and are the safe way to snapshot terrain; get_used_paint_layer_info_objects/get_used_paint_layer_names are editor-only (DevelopmentOnly) and return nothing at runtime. GOTCHAS: game-thread only; heights are stored across R+G for 16-bit so prefer RTF_RGBA16f/32f and matching rg-channel flags to avoid precision loss; Z-scale formula is (max height in meters)*100*0.001953125 (XY/Z all in cm); edit-layer merge is async (BatchedMerge) so you must flush/save before reading back; wrap edits in ScopedEditorTransaction and save the actor's package. UE5.7 deprecations: ELandscapeEditLayersMergeMode, GetObsoleteEditLayersInComponents (use RemoveObsoleteEditLayers on ALandscape or DeleteLayer), and several LODDistribution setters.
notes.LandscapeProxy: Base class for landscape actors and the per-streaming-proxy (ALandscapeStreamingProxy) pieces a World-Partition landscape is split into; ALandscape inherits from it. The two methods that matter for scripting are landscape_import_heightmap_from_render_target(render_target, import_height_from_rg_channel=False, edit_layer_index=0) and landscape_import_weightmap_from_render_target(render_target, layer_name, edit_layer_index=0) — both push a render target INTO the terrain (note the UE5.7 added edit_layer_index param), plus landscape_export_heightmap_to_render_target(render_target, export_height_into_rg_channel, export_landscape_proxies) to read it back. editor_apply_spline(...) carves splines into a named edit layer. GOTCHAS: marked UnsafeDuringActorConstruction; game-thread only and triggers shader/grass recompute, so batch and wrap in ScopedSlowTask; on World Partition landscapes you usually want the ALandscape (set export_landscape_proxies=True) rather than iterating proxies; set LandscapeMaterial/components dirty and save the proxy package, and guard re-runs by checking whether the target render target/heightmap already matches so you don't force a full re-import every run.
notes.InstancedFoliageActor: The per-level actor that stores all painted foliage as HierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponents; it is hidden from get_all_level_actors so fetch it with the static get_instanced_foliage_actor_for_current_level(world, create_if_none=True) (or ...for_level). READ path (works anywhere): get_used_foliage_types() then get_instance_transforms(foliage_type, level) — nested containers can't be returned so you must call both. WRITE path is the static AddInstances(world_context, foliage_type, transforms_array) / RemoveAllInstances(world_context, foliage_type) — CRITICAL: these are WITH_EDITOR-only, so they exist in editor Python but NOT in cooked/PIE runtime; for runtime spawning use FoliageHelper or add directly to an ISMC instead. GOTCHAS: game-thread only; transforms are FTransform with location in cm and rotation in degrees; wrap bulk adds in ScopedEditorTransaction and a ScopedSlowTask (thousands of instances stall Slate); the Foliage editor mode UI does not auto-refresh after script edits; under World Partition foliage is partitioned on a 256 m grid so there are MULTIPLE foliage actors per region — don't assume a single InstancedFoliageActor0. Idempotency: RemoveAllInstances(type) before re-AddInstances, or you double-paint on every re-run.
notes.FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh: The concrete UFoliageType asset wrapping a static mesh for foliage painting/instancing; this is what you pass to InstancedFoliageActor.add_instances. Create one in /Game with AssetTools and set its mesh via the 'mesh' editor property (or set_static_mesh / get_static_mesh); 'component_class' lets you swap in a custom FoliageInstancedStaticMeshComponent subclass, and there are separate material_overrides and nanite_material_overrides arrays. The placement/scatter knobs live on the parent UFoliageType: 'density' (instances per 1000x1000 uu = per 1 sq m at 100 uu/m, only used by paint/procedural scatter), 'radius' (min spacing in uu), 'scale_x/y/z' (FFloatInterval), 'z_offset', 'align_to_normal', 'random_yaw', plus cull_distance for LOD. GOTCHAS: game-thread; changing 'mesh' refires OnFoliageTypeMeshChanged and rebuilds existing instances, so set mesh first then add instances; save the asset package (default only_if_is_dirty=True); 'density'/'radius' do nothing for explicit add_instances (they only drive painting), so don't expect them to thin a transform list you supply yourself. Idempotency: does_asset_exist before recreating so you don't trigger a needless mesh rebuild.
notes.PCGComponent: The actor component that runs a PCG graph and owns the generated output; the entry point for driving Procedural Content Generation from Python. Assign work with set_graph(graph_interface) then trigger with generate(force=True) / generate_local(force) and clear with cleanup(remove_components) / cleanup_local(remove_components); after mutating exposed graph params at runtime call notify_properties_changed_from_blueprint() to dirty + auto-regenerate (plain generate alone won't pick up param changes). clear_pcg_link(template) bakes generated resources out to a standalone actor and severs the PCG link. GOTCHAS: PYTHON IS EDITOR-ONLY — you can script generate/cleanup for editor/pipeline automation but the component's actual gameplay-time generation must be C++/Blueprint; the editor Python you write cannot run in PIE/cooked. Generation is async/deferred (generate_local 'will be delayed'), so don't read outputs on the next line — hook on_pcg_graph_generated_external or wait. For runtime worlds set generation_trigger = GenerateAtRuntime (proximity-based via Generation Radii) or GenerateOnDemand; the default GenerateOnLoad only bakes at editor load. is_component_partitioned splits work across a grid (PCGWorldActor grid size unless the graph uses Hierarchical Generation). game-thread; save the owning actor after baking. UE5.6 deprecation: CleanupLocal overloads that took a bSave parameter (use the no-bSave versions).
notes.PCGGraph: The PCG graph ASSET (UPCGGraph) — the node network a PCGComponent executes; build/edit it programmatically then point a component at it. Key methods: add_node_of_type(settings_class) -> (node, default_settings) and add_node_instance/add_node_copy to place nodes, add_edge(from_node, from_pin_label, to_node, to_pin_label) to wire them (pin labels are FNames like 'In'/'Out'), remove_node(s), and get_input_node()/get_output_node() for the graph's fixed In/Out endpoints. get_nodes() lists current nodes. GOTCHAS: game-thread, editor-only; this is a saved asset so wrap structural edits in a transaction and save the package (changes invalidate the graph's cooked compilation data, forcing recompile/regeneration on every component that references it — expensive at scale, so batch). Pin labels must match the node settings' actual pin names or add_edge silently no-ops. After editing the graph, dependent PCGComponents need a regenerate (they react to graph changes unless only_track_itself is set). For most asset-pipeline work you build the graph once and reuse it via component.set_graph rather than rebuilding per run, so guard with does_asset_exist for idempotency.
notes.RuntimeVirtualTexture: The RVT *asset* (UObject, not an actor) that defines the virtual texture layout: what the texture stores and at what resolution. Configure it once, then reference it from a RuntimeVirtualTextureComponent. The properties that matter are set via `set_editor_property`: `material_type` (ERuntimeVirtualTextureMaterialType, e.g. `BASE_COLOR_NORMAL_SPECULAR`, `BASE_COLOR_NORMAL_ROUGHNESS`, `WORLD_HEIGHT`, `DISPLACEMENT`), `tile_count`, `tile_size`, and `tile_border_size` — note these four are flagged BlueprintReadOnly in the header so their BP *getters* are read-only, but `set_editor_property` still writes them (they are EditAnywhere). CRITICAL: these are LOG2 exponents, not literal sizes — actual resolution = `(1<<tile_count)*(1<<(tile_size+6))`; tile_size is clamped so the real tile edge is 64–1024 texels, tile_border = `2*clamp(tile_border_size,0,4)`. Use the read-only helpers `get_size()` and `get_page_table_size()` to see the resolved dimensions rather than guessing. Other useful EditAnywhere props: `compress_textures`, `remove_low_mips`, `adaptive` (for very large resolutions), `lod_group`. Gotchas: changing any of these makes every referencing component's streaming texture stale (rebuild required); `size`/`streaming_texture` properties named `Size_DEPRECATED`/`StreamingTexture_DEPRECATED` exist in the asset and must be ignored. The C++ `Initialize()` overload without a FOnReInitDelegate is deprecated as of 5.6 (not relevant from Python). Edit on the game thread, wrap in `unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction`, and `save_asset` to persist.
notes.RuntimeVirtualTextureComponent: The SceneComponent (held by a RuntimeVirtualTextureVolume actor) that places an RVT asset into the world and defines its bounds + streaming. The only two BlueprintCallable methods are `invalidate(world_bounds, invalidate_priority)` — mark a region dirty so its pages re-render (use after moving/deforming geometry that writes to the RVT) — and `request_preload(world_bounds, level)`. Assign the asset via `set_editor_property('virtual_texture', rvt_asset)` (BlueprintReadOnly; C++ SetVirtualTexture isn't a UFUNCTION). CRITICAL GOTCHA: there is NO Python/Blueprint way to call "Set Bounds" or "Build" — `set_bounds_button` and `build_streaming_mips_button` are read-only Transient bool *placeholders* for detail-panel buttons, and the real `RuntimeVirtualTexture::SetBounds`/`BuildStreamedMips` functions are plain C++ in the VIRTUALTEXTURINGEDITOR module (VIRTUALTEXTURINGEDITOR_API, no UFUNCTION), unreachable from Python in 5.7. So size the volume by driving the actor transform directly: the RVT volume's origin is at the CORNER (not center), and actor scale is in world cm (1 unit = 1 cm, so 5 m = scale 500). Set mobility Movable, `set_actor_location(min_corner)` + `set_actor_scale3d(max-min)`, then restore Static. Streaming props worth setting: `stream_low_mips` (clamped 0–12), `streaming_texture` (a VirtualTextureBuilder), `lossy_compression_amount`, `snap_bounds_to_landscape`/`bounds_align_actor` for landscape alignment. Building the streaming mips themselves must be done interactively via the Build menu / details button, or via a C++ commandlet/exec — budget for that limitation in any automation. Game thread only; wrap edits in a transaction and save the level package.
notes.VirtualTextureBuilder: Container asset (DisplayName "Streaming Runtime Virtual Texture") that holds the baked low-mip UVirtualTexture2D streamed for an RVT — it's what the component's `streaming_texture` points at. From Python it is essentially a passive handle: read `texture`/`texture_mobile` (BlueprintReadOnly) and toggle `b_separate_texture_for_mobile`, but you CANNOT bake it from Python — `BuildTexture()` is `#if WITH_EDITOR` C++ only and not a UFUNCTION, so the data is produced exclusively by the editor's "Build Virtual Textures" / RVT-volume Build action (or a C++ build path). Use `get_virtual_texture(shading_path)` to fetch the resolved UVirtualTexture2D for a given EShadingPath. Gotcha: its FVirtualTextureBuildDesc field `bContinuousUpdate` is deprecated/unused as of 5.6. If you script RVT setup, create/assign this asset but expect a manual Build step; never assume editing component settings rebuilds it automatically (a warning icon appears in-editor when it goes stale).
notes.NiagaraSystem: The compiled FX asset (an emitter-graph container) you load with EAL.load_asset and feed to spawn calls or NiagaraComponent.set_asset(); you almost never edit its graph from Python (no scriptable emitter-editing API — that lives in the Niagara editor/UNiagaraScript internals). WHY/GOTCHA: a freshly imported or migrated system may have stale/uncompiled shaders and will silently spawn nothing until it compiles — open it once in-editor or check it is valid before relying on it at runtime; treat it as read-only config from scripts. Validate with `unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist` for idempotency rather than re-importing. Override per-instance behavior on the spawned NiagaraComponent, not on this shared asset.
notes.NiagaraComponent: The per-instance handle returned by the spawn library; this is where you push 'User.' exposed parameters and control playback. Prefer the FName setters `set_variable_float/vec3/linear_color/bool/int/position/actor/object` over the deprecated (UE5.3) FString `set_niagara_variable_*` string variants. CRITICAL ORDERING: spawn with auto_activate=False, set your User parameters, then call activate(reset=True) — setting variables after activation often misses the spawn-time initialization, so the system runs with defaults. Use set_asset(in_asset) to swap the template, deactivate()/destroy_component() to tear down. Game-thread only; positions are cm and rotations deg. Note UE5.5+ changed the Niagara coordinate handling, so verify Local Space vs World Space on the system if effects land at world origin.
notes.NiagaraFunctionLibrary: Static spawn/utility entry point. The two you actually call are `spawn_system_at_location(world_context_object, system_template, location, rotation, scale, auto_destroy, auto_activate, pooling_method, pre_cull_check)` and `spawn_system_attached(...)`; both need a VALID world_context_object (a level actor or the editor world via EditorActorSubsystem/UnrealEditorSubsystem.get_editor_world) — a null context is the #1 reason the call silently returns None. GOTCHA: components spawned from an editor (non-PIE) script live in the editor world and won't persist or tick like gameplay; for editor-time VFX prefer placing a NiagaraActor (with NiagaraComponent) via the actor-spawning subsystems instead of this transient spawn. Also exposes the `override_system_user_variable_*_component`/`set_*_data_interface*` helpers to bind meshes/textures by parameter name. Location is cm.
notes.AudioComponent: Plays a SoundBase at runtime; this is a RUNTIME object, not a content editor — its methods only produce audio when there is a live audio device/world (PIE or a real game world), so a plain Editor Utility script generally hears nothing. Core methods: set_sound(new_sound), play(start_time=0.0), stop(), fade_in/fade_out(duration, level, curve), set_paused(b), set_volume_multiplier(v). Push runtime params with set_float_parameter/set_bool_parameter/set_integer_parameter (MetaSound/SoundCue inputs). Game-thread only; durations in seconds. GOTCHA: don't try to author/save sound assets through this — to inspect an asset use SoundBase directly. FAudioComponentParam was deprecated in UE5.0 (use FAudioParameter); EnableSubmixSendsOnPreview deprecated in UE5.7.
notes.SoundBase: Base of every playable sound (SoundWave/SoundCue/MetaSoundSource/etc.); from Python it is mostly a READ-ONLY metadata handle you load with EAL.load_asset to inspect before wiring audio. Get length via the read-only `duration` property (`sound.get_editor_property('duration')` or `sound.duration`) NOT a method — the C++ GetDuration()/GetMaxDistance()/IsLooping() are not the idiomatic Python path. GOTCHA: `duration` can be INDEFINITELY_LOOPING (a huge sentinel float) for looping sounds, so check IsLooping/the loop flag before using it as a real length. You don't 'play' a SoundBase directly — assign it to an AudioComponent.set_sound() or pass to GameplayStatics spawn-sound helpers. No game-thread editing concern since you only read it.
notes.AnimSequence: Skeletal animation clip. EDITING IS NON-OBVIOUS in UE5.x: do not poke the legacy fields — almost everything (NumFrames, SequenceLength, RawAnimationData, SamplingFrameRate) is deprecated (5.0+) behind the source-data model. To read length use get_play_length(); to mutate keys/length/framerate go through the controller: `controller = anim_seq.get_controller()`, wrap edits in `controller.open_bracket('desc')` ... `controller.close_bracket()` (this batches notifies + makes one undo step + avoids per-edit recompression), then EAL.save_loaded_asset to persist. Use SetNumberOfFrames (SetPlayLength deprecated 5.1) and AddBoneCurve/SetBoneTrackKeys (AddBoneTrack returning index deprecated 5.2). Read source via get_data_model_interface() (the old data_model property is superseded). bEnableRootMotion gates root motion; ExtractRootMotion* now require an FAnimExtractContext (old overloads deprecated 5.6). Editor/game-thread only; times in seconds, keys in cm/quat.
notes.AnimMontage: A montage = an AnimComposite with named Sections + Slot tracks, used to trigger animations on a live character. From Python the asset itself only offers QUERY helpers worth caring about: get_section_index(name)->int (-1 if absent), get_section_name(index), get_section_length(index), get_num_sections(), get_default_blend_in/out_time(). CRITICAL: you do NOT play or jump sections on the montage asset — playback lives on unreal.AnimInstance at runtime (montage_play, montage_jump_to_section, montage_get_current_section), so a pure editor script can inspect structure but cannot drive it. composite_sections/slot_anim_tracks are arrays; BlendInTime/BlendOutTime fields are deprecated in favor of the FAlphaBlend BlendIn/BlendOut. Authoring montage sections/slots from Python is not well-supported — build them in the editor. Times in seconds.
notes.LevelSequence: The cinematic asset (a UMovieSceneSequence subclass) that holds bindings, tracks, and a playback range. You almost never call methods ON the instance directly: its own surface is just metadata/user-data; all the useful scripting verbs (get_movie_scene, get_bindings, find_binding_by_name, add_possessable, add_track, find_tracks_by_type, get/set_playback_start/end, get/set_display_rate, make_range) are HOISTED from MovieSceneSequenceExtensions, so call them as unreal.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions.get_bindings(seq) OR just seq.get_bindings(seq)-style via the extension. Create one idempotently with EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist first, then AssetTools.create_asset(name, '/Game/Path', unreal.LevelSequence, unreal.LevelSequenceFactoryNew()); persist edits with EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset (the asset is dirtied by track/section edits). Gotcha: editing bindings does NOT auto-refresh the open Sequencer panel — call LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary.refresh_current_level_sequence() after mutations, and all of this must run on the game thread.
notes.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions: The static function library that supplies nearly all LevelSequence scripting verbs — methods are 'hoisted' onto the sequence so you pass the sequence as the first arg. The few you actually need: get_movie_scene(seq), get_bindings(seq)/find_binding_by_name(seq, name) to reach a MovieSceneBindingProxy, add_track(seq, track_type)+add_section() for master/object tracks, get/set_playback_start(seq,frame) & ..._end (frame-based) or the _seconds variants, get/set_display_rate (FrameRate, e.g. 30/1) and get_tick_resolution (the underlying high-res tick grid — frame numbers you pass to set_range are in TICKS, not display frames, unless you convert via make_range/make_range_seconds). CRITICAL UE5.7 DEPRECATIONS: add_spawnable_from_class/_instance -> use LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem instead; add/set/get/find_marked_frame -> use the overload that takes a MovieSceneTimeUnit (default DISPLAY_RATE) instead; legacy add_master_track/find_master_tracks_* -> use add_track/find_tracks_by_*. Game-thread only; remember to save the owning asset afterward.
notes.CineCameraActor: An ACameraActor subclass whose entire camera behavior lives on its CineCameraComponent — get it with actor.get_cine_camera_component() (NOT the generic camera_component) and set lens/filmback/focus there, not on the actor. The actor itself mainly adds look_at_tracking (LookatTrackingSettings: enable_look_at_tracking + actor_to_track soft ptr) for auto-aiming at a target. When scripting cinematics, prefer creating it as a Sequencer spawnable via LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem.create_camera(spawnable=True) — that also adds the camera-cut track in one call — rather than spawning a loose level actor. Transform is cm/degrees like any actor. Wrap level mutations in unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction and run on the game thread; for an existing actor call modify() before changing tracked properties so undo/dirty state is correct.
notes.CineCameraComponent: Where real photographic camera settings live. Key nested-struct properties (set via set_editor_property with a fresh struct, then assign back — structs are value types, so mutate-in-place won't stick): filmback (CameraFilmbackSettings: sensor_width/sensor_height in MILLIMETERS, e.g. 36x24 full-frame), lens_settings (CameraLensSettings: min/max_focal_length & min/max_f_stop in mm / f-stop), focus_settings (CameraFocusSettings: focus_method = unreal.CameraFocusMethod.MANUAL/TRACKING/DISABLE/DO_NOT_OVERRIDE, manual_focus_distance in CENTIMETERS). Scalar Interp props for keyframing: current_focal_length (mm, drives FOV — there is no direct FOV setter, set focal length), current_aperture (f-stop). UNIT TRAP: focal length & sensor are mm, but manual_focus_distance and the scene are cm — don't mix. current_focus_distance and current_horizontal_fov are READ-ONLY (control them via focus_settings / focal length); query FOV with get_horizontal_field_of_view(). Presets: set_filmback_preset_by_name / set_lens_preset_by_name. UE5.7 deprecation: per-component filmback/lens preset list getters (get_filmback_presets, get_default_filmback_preset_name, etc.) are deprecated since 5.1 — read presets from the UCineCameraSettings object instead. Game-thread only.
notes.Paths: Static helper (no instance) for resolving on-disk directories and doing pure string path math; it does NOT touch assets — `/Game/...` content-browser paths are a different namespace (use EditorAssetLibrary/SoftObjectPath for those). The methods that matter: `project_dir()`, `project_content_dir()`, `project_saved_dir()`, `engine_dir()` to anchor file IO (logs, exports, temp JSON), and `combine([a, b, c])` (takes a LIST, not varargs) plus `get_clean_filename`/`get_base_filename`/`get_path`/`get_extension`/`normalize_filename` for splitting. Returned paths use forward slashes and are usually relative to the project root — call `convert_relative_path_to_full(p)` before handing them to non-UE tools or os/open(). Use `file_exists`/`directory_exists` for idempotency guards before writing. Gotchas: these are filesystem paths in cm-agnostic land (no units), safe off the game thread for pure string ops, but anything that writes files should still run on the game thread in editor scripts; do NOT use these to build asset reference strings. UE5.7: legacy `game_dir`/`game_content_dir` aliases are gone (use the `project_*` forms); a few niche dirs were deprecated in 5.4/5.5 (platform-extension dirs, cooked-editor localization) but none of the common project/engine accessors changed.
notes.EditorFilterLibrary: Editor-only static utility (requires the EditorScriptingUtilities plugin enabled) for whittling down arrays of level Actors/Objects you already fetched — it is purely functional: every method returns a NEW filtered list and never mutates the input, so you must capture the return value and can chain them (by_class → by_actor_label → by_actor_tag). The 4 that matter: `by_class(array, klass, filter_type)`, `by_actor_label(array, name_sub_string, string_match, filter_type, ignore_case=True)` (label = the human name in the Outliner, NOT the internal id), `by_actor_tag(array, tag, filter_type)`, and `by_id_name(...)` (internal object id). Control matching with `unreal.EditorScriptingStringMatchType` (CONTAINS default / MATCHES_WILDCARD for patterns like 'Wall_*' / EXACT_MATCH) and inclusion with `unreal.EditorScriptingFilterType` (INCLUDE default / EXCLUDE to invert). Gotchas: must run on the game thread and not in PIE; tag/layer/level args are FName so pass plain strings (auto-coerced, case-insensitive); these only filter — they do not select or modify actors, so no transaction/save is needed here, but the source array should come from `unreal.EditorActorSubsystem().get_all_level_actors()` (the old EditorLevelLibrary is deprecated). For large/Tick-frequency filtering a manual comprehension can be faster; otherwise prefer this for readability.
notes.Name: The Python wrapper for C++ FName — an interned, immutable, CASE-INSENSITIVE identifier used for tags, bone/socket names, row names, and many FName-typed properties. In practice you almost never construct it explicitly: anywhere an FName is expected (function args like `by_actor_tag`, or `set_editor_property('some_fname_prop', 'Foo')`) a plain Python `str` is auto-coerced, so reach for `unreal.Name("Foo")` only when you need an explicit object or to compare/normalize. Useful methods: `is_none()` (equals NAME_None, the 'unset' sentinel) and `is_valid()`. Gotchas: because comparison is case-insensitive, 'Wall' and 'wall' match — do not rely on FName to preserve or distinguish case; it is a label, not free text (no substring/concat ops — convert to str first). It is a cheap value type with no editor side effects, so no game-thread/transaction concerns for the Name itself; those apply to whatever property you set it on.
notes.SoftObjectPath: Wrapper for FSoftObjectPath — a serializable, lazy reference to an asset (or subobject) by path string, WITHOUT loading it; this is the right type for storing/passing 'which asset' in tooling and for setting soft-reference properties. Construct from a path string `unreal.SoftObjectPath('/Game/Folder/Asset.Asset')` (note the duplicated name after the dot = the 'object path' form; the bare package name also works). Key methods: `to_string()`, `get_long_package_name()`, `get_asset_name()`, `is_null()`/`is_valid()`, and `try_load()` / `resolve_object()` to actually pull the UObject into memory (try_load loads if needed, resolve_object only returns it if already loaded). Best practice: when iterating many assets, query the Asset Registry and read `unreal.AssetData` metadata (class/name/path) WITHOUT loading; only call `try_load()` when you need the live object — and prefer `asset_data.to_soft_object_path()` over hand-building path strings to avoid format errors. For one-off loads by known string, `unreal.load_asset('/Game/...')` or `EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(...)` (load-if-needed) are simpler than going through this type. Gotchas: loading is expensive and game-thread/blocking; not for level assets via EditorAssetLibrary; FTopLevelAssetPath is the serialize-only cousin that canNOT load. UE5.6+ deprecations carried into 5.7: the `(package_name, asset_name)` constructor is deprecated (use FTopLevelAssetPath) and `get_sub_path_string()` is deprecated in favor of `get_sub_path_utf8_string()`.
